transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends — this is a decision-bearing review, so we're not deferring approval. The legacy API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit 98 percent of observed traffic, so it's well past our migration-readiness threshold. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can settle on this, our standard deprecation review requires both the API engineer and customer success to formally disclose any newly confirmed evidence through the review record — a verbal acknowledgement alone doesn't complete that check. So let's hear from both of you. What evidence or concerns do you need to put on the record?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to disclose this on the record: Minutes ago, while investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest of these integrators needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I haven't updated the deprecation ticket yet because I only confirmed the traffic identities just now. This directly impacts the current draft plan — the 7-day notice and 7-day overlap window won't be sufficient for at least one of these integrators.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to formally disclose this on the record: I confirmed with the account team this morning that the Northstar contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. The customer record hasn't been updated yet because this confirmation came from a contract attachment I was reviewing for another renewal. This directly impacts the draft plan — the 7-day notice and 7-day overlap are far short of Northstar's contractual requirements.
